question: what does the model learn in zero-shot setting?

extractive_spans: we simply adopted the official training script of BERT, with default hyperparameters, to fine-tune each model until training loss converged
evidence: We have training and testing sets in three different languages: English, Chinese and Korean. The English dataset is SQuAD BIBREF2. The Chinese dataset is DRCD BIBREF14, a Chinese RC dataset with 30,000+ examples in the training set and 10,000+ examples in the development set. The Korean dataset is KorQuAD BIBREF15, a Korean RC dataset with 60,000+ examples in the training set and 10,000+ examples in the development set, created in exactly the same procedure as SQuAD. We always use the development sets of SQuAD, DRCD and KorQuAD for testing since the testing sets of the corpora have not been released yet.

The pre-trained multi-BERT is the official released one. This multi-lingual version of BERT were pre-trained on corpus in 104 languages. Data in different languages were simply mixed in batches while pre-training, without additional effort to align between languages. When fine-tuning, we simply adopted the official training script of BERT, with default hyperparameters, to fine-tune each model until training loss converged.

title: Zero-shot Reading Comprehension by Cross-lingual Transfer Learning with Multi-lingual Language Representation Model
answer_short: The model learns to identify answer spans in context but less accurately, and it does not rely solely on language-independent strategies.
answer_rationale: The document discusses what the model learns in a zero-shot setting by analyzing its performance and internal representations. It states that the model can roughly identify answer spans but with less accuracy (Text 14). Additionally, experiments with unseen languages and code-switching datasets show that the model does not rely solely on language-independent strategies (Text 22, Text 27).
